clue.text: First-class airman's return to a European capital

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the whole run of letters is read from the end

parts.note: A1 is the old shipping-register mark for first class, written here as AI
FO is a Flying Officer in the RAF, an airman; the possessive adds the S

explanation.surface: A top-flight pilot flies back home to one of Europe's capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the whole of AIFOS (A1 plus FO's) back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Minister's company accepted by a superior

indicators.note: a thing accepted by someone is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a subdean is a cathedral officer who ranks above the canons and other clergy

explanation.surface: A government minister's firm is taken on by a senior official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks political, but here it means a clergyman; a subdean ranks just under a cathedral dean but above the canons.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdeacon is a cleric in minor orders who assists at the altar, so he is a minister of the church.

clue.text: Loud breather had a shy appearance

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction meaning loud
a lung is the organ you breathe with

explanation.surface: Someone breathing noisily looked timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' is the noun meaning a throw, as in a coconut shy at a British fair, not the adjective meaning timid; 'appearance' rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a shy is to throw something, and flung is the past tense of throw's synonym fling.

clue.text: Sufficient for a daughter to regard as similar

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees
to equate two things is to treat them as the same

explanation.surface: Enough for a girl to think two things alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an amount that is enough for the need.

clue.text: Abandoned type petting outside university

indicators.note: one piece is placed outside the other, so it wraps around it

parts.note: fondling is stroking or caressing, the same as petting

explanation.surface: A neglected sort of person caressing a partner off campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned type' reads like a description of a wanton person, but it means an abandoned baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundling is a baby left by its parents and found by strangers, an abandoned child.

clue.text: Dull character on the staff

definitions.meaning: dull in the sense of lifeless, monotonous
the musical sign that lowers a note by a semitone, written on the stave

explanation.definitionFit: A dull performance is lifeless and level; a symbol on a musical stave lowering a note a semitone has the same name.

clue.text: Gangsters supporting our environment?

parts.note: what supports something lies under it
the world is the environment we all live in

explanation.surface: Criminals propping up the planet we live on.
explanation.definitionFit: The criminal underworld is the collective name for organised criminals.

clue.text: Last month medical specialization appeared proper

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the final month of the year
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a branch of medicine

explanation.surface: A medical speciality turned up last month and seemed respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeared' only joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent and proper both mean respectable and in keeping with accepted standards.

clue.text: Inked it anew — it's a police representation

indicators.note: something done anew is made over again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the it of it's adds a second IT to the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Inking a drawing again to produce a police likeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anew' rearranges INKEDIT plus the second IT, nine letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: An Identikit is a composite picture of a suspect built from features, used by police.

clue.text: Someone's plans are ruined by her cooking

definitions.text: Someone's plans are ruined by her cooking

parts.words: Someone's plans are ruined by her cooking
parts.note: the idiom about wrecking a person's plans names a female bird that is cooked

explanation.definitionFit: To cook someone's goose is to spoil their plans, and the goose is the female of the bird.

clue.text: Laboured vigorously at first, rebuilding a road

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the same materials together in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
at first points to the opening letter of the word vigorously

explanation.surface: Someone worked hard at the start of rebuilding a highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives V from 'vigorously', and 'rebuilding' rearranges LABOURED plus V.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulevard is a broad city street, often tree-lined, so it is a kind of road.

clue.text: Concern about Trotskyist beliefs

indicators.note: one piece goes about, or around, the other

parts.note: a concern is a business, and CO is the abbreviation for company
a Trotskyist is a revolutionary communist, a red

explanation.surface: Worry over a Trotskyist's political views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' looks like worry but means a business firm; red is a common shorthand for any communist.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith, the set of things a person believes.

clue.text: Its contents are formed in a single layer

definitions.text: Its contents are formed in a single layer

parts.words: Its contents are formed in a single layer
parts.note: the contents are made in one laying by a hen, a single layer being one bird that lays

explanation.definitionFit: An eggcup holds a boiled egg, which a hen, a layer, has produced.

clue.text: The beast is about to catch Jeanie for one

indicators.note: the first piece is about, around, the second

parts.note: a brute is a savage beast
to net something is to catch it

explanation.surface: A wild animal is ready to seize a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeanie is the girl with the light brown hair in the Stephen Foster song, so she exemplifies the hair colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's Jeanie has light brown hair, making her a woman with dark hair, an example of the type.

clue.text: Supporter on burning issue has original thought

parts.note: a bra supports the bust
a fire that is in is still alight
issue means offspring, a child

explanation.surface: A supporter speaking on a hot topic has a fresh idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning issue' looks like a hot topic, but a fire that is 'in' is still alight, and issue means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainchild is an idea or invention that a person came up with themselves.

clue.text: Tax 'botcher may be a blatherskite

indicators.note: the letters may be put together into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who bungles tax returns might be a windbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges TAX and BOTCHER into ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A blatherskite is a person who talks foolishly at length, a non-stop talker.

clue.text: Where to make a branch inspection?

definitions.text: Where to make a branch inspection?

parts.words: Where to make a branch inspection?
parts.note: the branch looks like an office of a bank, but here it is part of a tree, inspected in a tree garden

explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a garden of trees grown for study, where boughs can be examined.

clue.text: Predator in the sky plagues Kuala Lumpur

annotationWithheld.why: Predator in the sky plagues Kuala Lumpur (4): the bird is hidden in 'plagueS KUAla', but no word signals the hidden run except 'plagues' itself, which also gives the S, so one word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Predator in the sky plagues Kuala Lumpur

clue.text: Stones are that messy, in ruins

indicators.note: something in ruins is wrecked and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Building stones that are untidy and lying in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethysts are purple quartz gemstones, a kind of precious stone.

clue.text: Roles revised after one member makes an earnest plea

indicators.note: after places the rearranged word behind the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: revised means altered and put into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor pleads to have the parts rewritten after one MP intervenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges the word roles; 'after' puts those letters behind I and MP.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beg someone desperately, an urgent request.

clue.text: Writer's his mock title

definitions.meaning: the points of a pen, the parts of a writing tool
the jokey honorific for a self-important man, as in his ...

explanation.definitionFit: Pen points are nibs, and calling a pompous man 'his nibs' mocks him with a fake title.

clue.text: Thoroughly modern girl grasps new term used in measurement

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Thoroughly Modern Millie is a 1967 film musical about a flapper

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fashionable young woman picks up a new word used in measuring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the word term and 'grasps' puts it inside the name; Thoroughly Modern Millie is the 1967 film musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A millimetre is a metric unit of length, a thousandth of a metre.

clue.text: A girl wrong about nothing (her and her halo!)

indicators.note: one piece goes about, or around, the other
wrong means put in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl mistaken about something trivial, with a remark about her glowing reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed exclamation is the definition: Gloria is a girl's name, so 'her', and a gloria is also a halo in religious art.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloria is a halo or aureole of light around a holy figure in art, and Gloria is a woman's name.

clue.text: Vestment they say you are wearing to marry

indicators.note: something wearing a thing has it on, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to splice is to join, and to get spliced is slang for to marry

indicators.note: they say signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: the words 'you are' said quickly sound like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: A garment worn by someone getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting spliced is old slang for getting married, and the vestment is the garment the clergyman wears at the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplice is a loose white linen robe worn over a cassock by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: Explosive satirical composition

definitions.meaning: a small firework that hisses and bangs
a short piece of writing that mocks its target

explanation.definitionFit: A squib is both a small firework and a short witty lampoon.

clue.text: This share gets several stars

definitions.meaning: a share is the blade of a farm implement, completing the compound word
the group of seven stars in Ursa Major known in Britain by a farming name

explanation.definitionFit: A ploughshare is the cutting blade of the farm tool, and the Plough is the British name for the Big Dipper.

clue.text: In the saddle, aim to stand erect

parts.note: a rider in the saddle is up on the horse
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Mounted on a horse, a rider tries to stand upright.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to set it on its end, standing it up vertically.

clue.text: A number beheaded in uniform

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: seven is a number

explanation.surface: A digit dressed in military kit loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and uniform both mean regular and unvarying throughout.

clue.text: Declare perfect

definitions.meaning: to declare is to speak out or say aloud
perfect in the sense of complete, absolute, as in total nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say something, and utter as an adjective means complete or total.

clue.text: Fashionable French writer's second cloak

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
Jules Verne was the French author of Around the World in Eighty Days; the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A stylish French author's second-best cape.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inverness is a sleeveless cape or a coat with a detachable cape, named after the Scottish town.

clue.text: Stop an order to persist in shelling

parts.note: to bombard is to shell with artillery
'on!' is a command to keep going, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Halt a command to keep up the artillery barrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like halt, but it means an organ stop; 'in' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardon is a deep reed stop on an organ, as well as a bass brass instrument.

clue.text: Superior air adopted by society pages

indicators.note: one thing adopted by another is taken on after it, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: side is British slang for a superior manner, as in putting on side

explanation.surface: Haughty manners taken up by the high-society columns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' as haughtiness is chiefly British, as in 'no side about him'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sides of a sheet of paper are its two faces, each one a page.
